melee.name: Supply Wrangler
melee.description: Gets up close with staplers, coffee mugs, rubber bands, and whatever the printer has jammed this time.

ranged.name: Comms Specialist
ranged.description: Deals damage from a safe distance with sarcastic emails, weaponized politeness, and corporate jargon.

ranged.name: Systems Hacker
ranged.description: Uses scripts, exploits, automation, and questionable fixes to bend company systems to the team's needs.

healer.name: Help Desk
healer.description: Restores the team's health with troubleshooting, coffee, patient explanations, and the occasional reboot.

buff_and_debuff.name: Project Manager
buff_and_debuff.description: Shifts calendars, delegates strategically, and turns impossible deadlines into someone else's action item.

races.name: Developer
races.description: Builds and repairs the systems everyone depends on, often while insisting the bug is impossible to reproduce.
races.look: A tired office worker in a hoodie, badge, and jeans, with a laptop tucked under one arm and a coffee mug in hand. Their expression suggests they have spotted a bug nobody else can see.

races.name: Business Analyst
races.description: Translates what people ask for into what they might actually need, ideally before the requirements change again.
races.look: A neatly dressed office worker with a notebook, badge, and color-coded documents. They hold a marker poised over a diagram, wearing the focused look of someone clarifying a vague request.

races.name: Deadline Wrangler
races.description: Keeps meetings, deadlines, and stakeholders moving, even when nobody agrees on what the project is.
races.look: A business-casual worker with a badge, tablet, and packed calendar. They point toward a conference room while balancing a coffee and maintaining an encouraging, slightly strained smile.

races.name: Help-Desk Veteran
races.description: Can calm an angry user, recognize a familiar outage, and ask whether the computer has been restarted without losing composure.
races.look: A seasoned office worker wearing a headset and badge, with a practical sweater and a well-used mug. One hand gestures toward a monitor while the other reaches for a notepad.

races.name: Intern
races.description: Has little authority, boundless energy, and a surprising habit of finding the one setting nobody thought to check.
races.look: A young office worker with a fresh badge, slightly oversized business-casual clothes, and a laptop covered in simple stickers. They look alert and curious, holding a notebook full of questions.

races.name: Executive
races.description: Arrives with ambitious visions, limited implementation details, and complete confidence that IT can deliver by Friday.
races.look: A polished executive in a tailored suit and badge, holding a sleek tablet and gesturing toward an unseen presentation. Their confident smile suggests the project is already considered a success.

statuses.name: Coffee-Fueled
statuses.description: Break-room coffee turns routine effort into alarming productivity. The mug is technically company property.

statuses.name: Clean Build
statuses.description: A tested script and a passing review make the team more effective—and harder to surprise.

statuses.name: Strategic Delegation
statuses.description: Someone else owns the action items now. You have time to get out of the way.

statuses.name: Snack Break
statuses.description: A granola bar and five uninterrupted minutes restore stamina. The meeting can wait.

statuses.name: Meeting Creep
statuses.description: One agenda item becomes six. Leaving the conference room is somehow still on the agenda.

statuses.name: Reply-All Storm
statuses.description: Every response adds another notification, another misunderstanding, and another thing to investigate.

statuses.name: Scope Creep
statuses.description: Requirements keep changing, leaving every plan exposed to one more executive suggestion.

statuses.name: Printer Jam
statuses.description: The printer makes a new sound. Everyone stops to look, including the person who knows how to fix it.

statuses.name: Calendar Hold
statuses.description: A recurring invitation has claimed this time slot and refuses to acknowledge the conflict.

statuses.name: Corporate Mumble
statuses.description: A dense fog of alignment and strategic synergy makes clear communication temporarily impossible.

statuses.name: Lost Badge
statuses.description: The target cannot reach the supply closet, the server room, or the stapler they were absolutely about to use.

statuses.name: Paper Cut
statuses.description: A tiny injury with an outsized effect on typing, morale, and willingness to handle loose forms.

tier_1.name: Stapler Calibration
tier_1.description: A firm, practiced staple to the nearest problem. The stapler was working yesterday.

tier_1.name: Coffee Mug Lunge
tier_1.description: Close the distance with a company mug and the confidence of someone who knows where the spare mugs are.

tier_2.name: Rubber Band Volley
tier_2.description: An economical attack with excellent range and a concerning amount of prep time.

tier_2.name: Break-Room Refill
tier_2.description: The coffee is burnt, but it is available. Productivity resumes under protest.

tier_3.name: Printer Tray Slam
tier_3.description: Strike the printer at exactly the angle that makes the jam somebody else's problem.

tier_3.name: Rolling Chair Charge
tier_3.description: Roll into the fray, ignoring the posted warning and the one wheel that keeps catching.

tier_4.name: Office Supply Incident
tier_4.description: Deploy a stapler, two mugs, and a rubber band of undocumented provenance against nearby threats.

tier_1.name: Polite Follow-Up
tier_1.description: A courteous message that makes it clear the deadline was in the original email.

tier_1.name: Per My Last Email
tier_1.description: Quote the thread in full. No one is sure who started this, but everyone feels worse.

tier_2.name: Executive Summary
tier_2.description: Condense the issue into jargon so impenetrable that the enemy loses track of its own objection.

tier_2.name: Softly, Firmly
tier_2.description: A very polite correction that leaves no room for a useful interpretation.

tier_3.name: CC the Director
tier_3.description: Add the director to the thread. The sudden attention does wonders for compliance.

tier_3.name: Stakeholder Alignment
tier_3.description: Align everyone on the fact that the request is still changing. This somehow makes it worse.

tier_4.name: Reply-All Autopsy
tier_4.description: Reconstruct the entire thread, assigning responsibility with the calm precision of a forensic accountant.

tier_1.name: Quick Script
tier_1.description: Run a short script against the problem. It has been tested on something similar, probably.

tier_1.name: Credential Guess
tier_1.description: Try the password the department uses for everything. The audit can wait until after the outage.

tier_2.name: Dependency Audit
tier_2.description: Find the one package update nobody remembers approving and make it everyone's problem.

tier_2.name: Rollback Routine
tier_2.description: Restore the last known working version. It was three versions ago, but it worked.

tier_3.name: Automated Triage
tier_3.description: Sort the incoming chaos into queues. The queues are also on fire, but now they are labeled.

tier_3.name: Passing Build
tier_3.description: A clean test run gives the team a rare moment of confidence and a slightly safer script.

tier_4.name: Production Hotfix
tier_4.description: Patch the live system with a fix that works immediately and will be explained in the postmortem.

tier_1.name: Have You Rebooted
tier_1.description: A patient reboot resolves more crises than the company is prepared to acknowledge.

tier_1.name: Troubleshooting Steps
tier_1.description: Walk an ally through the fix one step at a time. It is not their fault the instructions are outdated.

tier_2.name: Water-Cooler Triage
tier_2.description: A brief check-in, a glass of water, and permission to stop staring at the error message.

tier_2.name: Unstick the Queue
tier_2.description: Clear the team's accumulated little problems before they become a very large spreadsheet.

tier_3.name: Emergency Reimage
tier_3.description: Restore an ally's system state from backup. Their desktop wallpaper is gone, but they are back.

tier_3.name: Coffee and Reassurance
tier_3.description: The coffee is terrible. The reassurance is sincere. Both are covered by the support contract.

tier_4.name: All-Hands Recovery
tier_4.description: Restore the team's health, clear lingering problems, and avoid mentioning the outage's original cause.

tier_1.name: Action Item Transfer
tier_1.description: Assign the awkward task to someone with a full calendar and a surprisingly reliable work ethic.

tier_1.name: Move the Check-In
tier_1.description: Reschedule the meeting to a time when the problem is, ideally, somebody else's.

tier_2.name: Revised Timeline
tier_2.description: Add a discovery phase, a review phase, and an ominous amount of red to the project plan.

tier_2.name: Motivational Slide
tier_2.description: Show a graph trending upward. No one checks what it measures, and morale improves slightly.

tier_3.name: Requirements Workshop
tier_3.description: Ask what success looks like until the request acquires three new requirements and no owner.

tier_3.name: No-Meeting Block
tier_3.description: Reserve focus time. The invitation is declined, then recreated by someone who did not read the title.

tier_4.name: Friday Commitment
tier_4.description: Convert the deadline into an action item, then assign it to the person who suggested Friday.

one_handed.name: Heavy-Duty Stapler
one_handed.description: A reliable close-range persuader. Its staple tray is empty, but the threat remains fully loaded.

two_handed.name: Jam-Prone Printer
two_handed.description: A hulking office printer wielded by its paper tray. Every swing comes with a fresh error message.

one_handed.name: Reply-All Email
one_handed.description: A concise, devastatingly polite message that reaches the whole distribution list.

two_handed.name: Quarterly Slide Deck
two_handed.description: A polished barrage of charts, jargon, and carefully worded implications, delivered from across the room.

one_handed.name: Hotfix USB
one_handed.description: A thumb drive full of quick fixes. Plugging it in is the fastest way to get dangerously close to the problem.

two_handed.name: Live Patch Console
two_handed.description: A portable terminal for hands-on exploits and urgent edits. The rollback plan is mostly optimism.

one_handed.name: Cron Job Launcher
one_handed.description: Schedules a small script to quietly disrupt a threat at a professionally reasonable distance.

two_handed.name: Distributed Botnet
two_handed.description: A fleet of questionable automations that floods the network with fixes and a few duplicate tickets.

one_handed.name: Break-Room Thermos
one_handed.description: Pours restorative coffee and delivers a sharp little caffeine jolt to whoever needs it.

two_handed.name: Snack Cart
two_handed.description: A rolling supply of coffee, granola bars, and practical check-ins. Also blocks a hallway at range.

one_handed.name: Status-Update Clicker
one_handed.description: Rallies allies with clear priorities or pins foes beneath a fresh list of action items.

two_handed.name: Master Project Calendar
two_handed.description: Moves deadlines, delegates strategically, and somehow schedules the enemy into back-to-back meetings.

shields.name: Oversized Coffee
shields.description: A sturdy mug of break-room coffee. Blocks trouble; contents may be older than the ticket.

shields.name: Insulated Travel Mug
shields.description: Keeps caffeine hot and incoming problems at arm's length through even the longest status meeting.

shields.name: Approved Expense Thermos
shields.description: A premium coffee vessel protected by procurement paperwork and a surprisingly strict reimbursement policy.

balanced.name: Business Casual
balanced.description: Standard office attire: presentable enough for leadership, comfortable enough for a long incident.

sturdy.name: Data Center Gear
sturdy.description: Layered, practical protection for server rooms and printer incidents. Heavy, warm, and not meeting-ready.

nimble.name: Friday Casual
nimble.description: Light, flexible clothes for dodging calendar invites and sprinting to the only working conference room.

Headset.name: Noise-Canceling Headset
Headset.description: Filters out open-office chatter and makes it easier to hear the one useful detail in a support call.

Headset.name: Help-Desk Headset
Headset.description: Always on, faintly crackling, and somehow still connected to the user who closed the ticket.

Mug.name: World's Okayest Mug
Mug.description: A chipped morale artifact that holds coffee and communicates realistic expectations.

Mug.name: Unclaimed Mug
Mug.description: No one knows whose it is. Everyone avoids asking, which gives it a strange authority.

Lanyard.name: All-Access Lanyard
Lanyard.description: Opens most doors, several supply closets, and one conference room nobody admits exists.

Lanyard.name: Conference Swag Lanyard
Lanyard.description: A tangle of old event badges that grants credibility in meetings and mild resistance to networking.

healing.name: Break-Room Emergency Kit
healing.description: Restores Health with a granola bar, a clean bandage, and five minutes nobody has booked yet.

cleansing.name: Incident Triage Checklist
cleansing.description: Removes harmful statuses. The checklist has been approved by someone who was not in the incident.

buffs.name: Mug of Unclear Origin
buffs.description: Break-room coffee turns routine effort into alarming productivity. The mug is technically company property.

buffs.name: Passing Test Suite
buffs.description: A tested script and a passing review make the team more effective—and harder to surprise.

buffs.name: Delegation Receipt
buffs.description: Someone else owns the action items now. You have time to get out of the way.

buffs.name: Emergency Granola Bar
buffs.description: A granola bar and five uninterrupted minutes restore stamina. The meeting can wait.

debuffs.name: Agenda Expansion
debuffs.description: One agenda item becomes six. Leaving the conference room is somehow still on the agenda.

debuffs.name: Reply-All Misfire
debuffs.description: Every response adds another notification, misunderstanding, and thing to investigate.

debuffs.name: One Tiny Revision
debuffs.description: Requirements keep changing, leaving every plan exposed to one more executive suggestion.

physical.name: Stapler With Intent
physical.description: Office damage delivered by a heavy-duty stapler whose service history is unavailable.

magic.name: Recursive Ticket Script
magic.description: Cyber damage from an automation script that opens tickets faster than anyone can close them.

valuables.name: Unclaimed Expense Receipt
valuables.description: A faded receipt for something nobody remembers buying. Finance may accept it as evidence.

valuables.name: Conference Room Key
valuables.description: Opens a room with a projector that works often enough to sustain hope.

valuables.name: Executive Approval Email
valuables.description: A rare written approval. It does not specify what was approved.

valuables.name: Vintage Access Badge
valuables.description: Belonged to an employee whose department was renamed three reorganizations ago.

valuables.name: Spreadsheet of Record
valuables.description: The authoritative tracker, according to three people who each maintain a different copy.

craft.name: Office Gear Assembly
craft.description: Make practical equipment from office supplies, documented exceptions, and whatever the supply closet has left.

brew.name: Break-Room Concessions
brew.description: Prepare consumables from coffee, snacks, and ingredients whose best-before dates are merely advisory.

upgrade.name: Process Improvement
upgrade.description: Strengthen gear with tested fixes, better parts, and a change request nobody has challenged yet.

enchant.name: Configuration Drift
enchant.description: Give gear a random new property through scripts, settings, and a careful refusal to ask why it works.

hard.name: Office Hardware
hard.description: Staplers, brackets, spare keys, and other sturdy parts for tools and shields.

soft.name: Supply Closet Stock
soft.description: Lanyards, foam, sleeves, and other soft goods for protective gear and accessories.

essence.name: Configuration Notes
essence.description: Half-documented settings and useful fragments of institutional knowledge for gear modifications.

reagent.name: Break-Room Supplies
reagent.description: Coffee, tea, snacks, and powdered creamer for making consumables.

art.artStyle: Handcrafted claymation, tactile fingerprints and soft fabric textures, expressive characters and exaggerated physical comedy, muted beige office surroundings contrasted with playful teal and coral accents, soft practical lighting, dry affectionate humor
